scenario: A wealth inequality study uses survey data that only captures households with net worth above $500,000, as the survey was distributed through high-net-worth banking channels. A policy researcher uses the survey's average wealth to model inequality.

data.description: Survey captures households with net worth > $500k only. Net worth assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $300k.

question: The survey reports a mean household net worth of $900k. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean household net worth Î¼ across the full population, and (b) the fraction of households captured by the survey.
naive_answer: The average household net worth is approximately $900k since that is the survey figure.
naive_trap: The survey misses the bottom 14% of the wealth distribution below $500k. The true population mean is about $79k lower at $821k. Using $900k to calibrate inequality models would understate the gap between the surveyed population and those below the threshold.

python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(500-mu)/300; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+300*norm.pdf(a)/sf-900 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,100,899)
assert abs(mu-821)<8
assert abs(norm.sf((500-mu)/300)-0.8580)<0.01
